ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, S is closed. It is known that the capacitance C=2μF, the electromotive force of the power supply E=12V, the internal resistance is neglected, R₁=1Ω, R₂=2Ω, R₃=6Ω, R₄=3Ω. Find the amount of charge carried by capacitor plate a.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the left end is node A, and the right end is node B; between A and B there are two upper and lower resistor branches. The upper branch is, in order, R1, node C, R2; the lower branch is, in order, R3, node D, R4. The capacitor is connected vertically between C and D, with the upper plate labeled a and the lower plate labeled b. The bottom power supply E and switch S are connected between A and B, and the problem states that S is closed and the internal resistance of the power supply is neglected. Then reason: after the switch is closed and stability is reached, there is no constant current in the capacitor branch, so the capacitor branch can first be disconnected, and only the two resistor branches between A and B are calculated. The power supply makes the voltage between A and B be 12V. The total resistance of the upper branch is R1+R2=1Ω+2Ω=3Ω, so the current I_top=12V/3Ω=4A. The voltage drop from A to C through R1 is I_top R1=4A×1Ω=4V, therefore V_C=V_A-4V. The total resistance of the lower branch is R3+R4=6Ω+3Ω=9Ω, so the current I_mid=12V/9Ω=4/3A. The voltage drop from A to D through R3 is I_mid R3=(4/3)A×6Ω=8V, therefore V_D=V_A-8V. Thus the voltage across the capacitor is U_ab=V_C-V_D=(V_A-4V)-(V_A-8V)=4V, and the potential of plate a is higher. The amount of charge carried by capacitor plate a is Q_a=C U_ab=2μF×4V=8×10^-6C, a positive charge.
